flagged.evidence: The item assumes only “A commuting square of first maps between two standard cone triangles” in K(A), then asserts: “The square of chain maps induces the block-diagonal map of mapping cones.” Equality of the square in K(A) means bf and f'a are chain-homotopic, not necessarily equal as chain maps. The cited dependency thm-a-morphism-of-chain-maps-induces-a-chain-map-of-cones applies only to a strict square satisfying bf = ga. A homotopy correction in the cone map is required, and the block-diagonal map need not be a chain map.

The proof cites only the dependency statement “Cone(f[1]) ≅ Cone(f)[1]” and concludes that “the signed left rotation of the standard cone triangle is isomorphic ... to a standard cone triangle for the shifted map.” The rotated triangle has terms D → Cone(f) → C[1] → D[1], whereas the standard cone triangle of f[1] has terms C[1] → D[1] → Cone(f[1]) → C[2]. The displayed cone-shift isomorphism does not supply an isomorphism of these triangles. Establishing TR2 instead requires analysis of the cone of D → Cone(f), which is absent.

The proof says: “Apply TR3 to the identity triangle and its sum with the zero triangle.” TR3 completes a commutative square of first arrows; it does not assert that a direct sum of distinguished triangles is distinguished. That direct-sum closure is a separate consequence requiring a construction, and no such construction or dependency is given here.

The proof says that “applying the chosen translation and its quasi-inverse to the resulting rotated triangles gives every integral translate.” A category-with-translation structure does not itself say that its translation preserves distinguished triangles. This must be derived from repeated signed rotations and an isomorphism with the translate; that derivation is omitted.
